hero: Your NZB files point to pieces of files stored on Usenet, and those pieces disappear over time. nzbs.live checks every one of them each month and tells you which are gone.
One check per article, on the 1st of every month
forgets: How an NZB works
Usenet forgets, slowly
First, what an NZB actually is.
Know how Usenet works? Skip ahead
It starts with an NZB
A small file from an indexer, a few hundred kilobytes. You hand it to your downloader and get a whole film back.
Behind it, one big file
The NZB stands for a film, an ISO or an archive, many gigabytes. On Usenet that file never travels in one piece.
Cut into articles
Before it is posted, the file is packed into parts, and every part is cut into small pieces called articles. Repair files, par2, travel with them.
Spread across Usenet
Every article is posted on its own, with a name of its own: its Message-ID. Usenet providers keep the copies.
The NZB is only the list
So the NZB you started with does not contain the film. It is a map: every Message-ID, and where each piece belongs. That is all.
Your downloader puts it back
SABnzbd or NZBGet read the map, fetch every article and join the pieces into the file again.
Then Usenet forgets
Providers drop articles over time, when retention runs out or a takedown removes them. The NZB never changes. The pieces it points to do.
One gap is enough
With pieces gone, the file cannot be joined. par2 repair data covers a few gaps, until there are too many. Your downloader finds out at 97%.
early: The first night an article goes missing, you still have options: par2 covers a small gap, or you grab another NZB while one is still around. Found by your downloader months later, at 97%, there are none left.
prom: Watch how your uploads hold up
Upload to Usenet yourself? nzbs.live has a Prometheus exporter. Every NZB becomes a line in your graphs, so you see which uploads are fading and replace them before they sink.
# HELP nzbs_live_nzb_availability Available unique articles / unique articles, last run
Straight into Grafana, Alertmanager or the dashboards you already use.
notify: One message, when the check is done
A few minutes after midnight on the 1st, nzbs.live sends one short message: how many NZBs lost articles, and how many articles. On a quiet month it tells you everything is good.

start: Usenet keeps forgetting. Now you know.
Add your NZBs once. On the 1st of every month nzbs.live checks every article, keeps every result and tells you what went missing.

forgets: An NZB file. A block of cubes, the file it stands for, grows out of it, then comes apart into its parts and articles, which scatter. The NZB is a list of them. A downloader joins them again, until articles drop out and the file cannot be joined.
early: The same NZB as a block of articles on five monthly nights, July to November. In July one article is gone and the light is on it; by November 46 of 70 are gone.
prom: Nine NZBs as lines across a year of monthly checks. Two sink below the waterline at 0.99, Caminandes in July and Spring.2019 in November.
notify: A phone lock screen at 00:06 on Sunday, 1 November, with the nzbs.live message from ntfy on top and last month's below
